headline: UK CMA proposes new rules for Android & Chrome, mandating search & AI assistant choices
summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority wants users to get yearly prompts for search engine choices on Android and Chrome, plus the ability to pick their preferred AI assistant.
details: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has proposed new measures to increase consumer choice for search engines on Android smartphones and the Chrome browser. The regulator aims to prevent Google's own search engine from being used automatically, requiring explicit user selection.

The proposal outlines three key recommendations. First, Google and Android phone makers would be forced to offer a choice of search platforms upon first use, followed by yearly reminders. Second, users would gain the ability to choose their preferred AI assistant, provided technical and security criteria are met.

Finally, the CMA seeks to mandate clearer attribution of publisher content by all search providers when displaying results, ensuring users can easily identify and access original sources. This move builds on existing UK rules that already allow search provider choice, but adds the new element of yearly prompts.

CMA chief executive Sarah Cardell stated the proposals are about "future-proofing the options available to people in the UK" as AI assistants become a more common search method. The CMA has been actively introducing new rules, including allowing publishers to opt out of AI results and imposing fair Google search ranking requirements.

While many regions, including Europe, already require initial search engine and browser choices, the focus on AI assistants is newer. Google's Gemini is currently deeply integrated into its search, but Apple has reportedly introduced hooks in upcoming macOS and iOS versions to allow third-party AI models to replace Siri's server, possibly anticipating similar regulatory changes.
